title: [CQ-RF05] daemon.json binding threat-model decision
definitionOfDone: A decision document under docs/ states whether same-user host processes are in the protected profile's threat model. It covers both the daemon.json port↔pid binding and the CQ-R08 per-request TOCTOU window.
It lists the options considered with reasons, records the decision, and names every follow-up row the decision requires. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md links it.
npm run lint exits 0 with its output supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.

implementationPlan.description:
PREMISE RE-CHECK, read-only (Serena find_symbol or grep; no edits, no Git writes, no scratch-repo reproduction). This is a re-plan: the first plan's step 1 failed, and comment-4bef8984 holds that evidence. The decision in step 2 already accounts for every fact below. Re-confirm each one and record the exact path:line plus symbol name the record will cite. Line numbers drift while peers land, so cite what you read.

F1. moe-jetbrains MoeDaemonSupervisor.readDaemonInfo (~:47) reads <project>/.moe/daemon.json. MoeProjectService.doConnect (~:247-264) connects to ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws. Under PROTECTED, activationRefusal → RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance (~:251) checks only the pid (start instant, or its direct parent). Nothing binds the port to that pid.
F2. scripts/local-runner/guest-session.mjs daemonRefusal (~:78-97):
- it runs before the spawn (~:66) and before every forward (~:173);
- it admits an absent bindHost or a literal loopback one (~:96).
Its header (~:1-8) says the guest gets no daemon address, port or token.
F3. packages/moe-daemon/src/server/WebSocketServer.ts: the WSS has no verifyClient (~:227). onConnection (~:289-310) attaches /mcp unauthenticated, authenticates only /runner, and treats every other path as a plugin client. No Origin handling exists in packages/moe-daemon/src unless task-801272c4 has landed; check its status.
F4. packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:
- probeDaemonHealth (~:302) trusts /health's self-reported pid, and picks its probe host from daemon.json's bindHost (~:314);
- validateDaemonInfoForProject is at ~:355;
- the host comes from --host or MOE_BIND_HOST (~:64);
- /health (~:669) reports no bind;
- daemon.json records bindHost only when it is not the default (~:769).
F5. A guest's loopback is its own. The guest path forwards no ports: bridgeArgv (scripts/local-runner/guest-bridge.mjs ~:204-207) is `multipass exec ... sudo -n <supervisor> bridge` over stdio. CQ-R13e (task-d00dafdf, not landed) is the row that certifies, on real hardware, that no guest reaches the host's daemon ports.
F6. Same-user host processes can already change the user-writable installed plugin and runtime, the owner-only IDE store (CQ-RF01), the IDE JVM and the daemon process (debugging, ptrace or OpenProcess), and node.
F7. .moe/daemon.json is gitignored (.gitignore:63). Git overwrites an ignored file when an upstream commit adds it: cite comment-4bef8984's reproduction and Serena memory gotcha-gitignored-moe-files-overwritten-by-pull, and do not re-run it.
F8. The same daemon.json bindHost admission sits in runner-client.mjs (~:48-50, RUNNER_DAEMON_NOT_LOOPBACK; it dials 127.0.0.1:<port>/runner at ~:107) and vm-control.mjs readDaemonInfo (~:116-131, with a /mcp dial at ~:140).
F9. packages/moe-daemon/src/server/runnerChannel.ts authenticateRunner admits only a loopback peer (isLoopback on remoteAddress) that presents the owner-only key from runnerKeyPath. A wide bind therefore does not expose /runner.
F10. Pending rows, by their task status (get_context or search_tasks): task-724e31fa, plus its slices task-801272c4 (Origin rule), task-2f2484b4 ('wsl' bind: loopback plus the WSL adapter) and task-0c72d59a (JetBrains passes --host wsl). Also task-2cf1c6be, this decision's new follow-up.
F11. WSL agent mode adds `--host 0.0.0.0` at protectedDaemonCommand (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt ~:222) and at both legacy builders (~:322, ~:336-337), unless task-0c72d59a has landed. TerminalAgentLauncher.isWslAgentsEnabled's doc (~:191-199) says the mode needs a bind beyond loopback.
F12. Under PROTECTED, TerminalAgentLauncher.resolveContext (~:267-268) still passes project.json's settings.agentCommand to the wrapper as --command, and moe-agent.sh runs it (parse_command_into_argv). This is R01's known gap; no open row covers it.

The following are already decided and are NOT stop conditions: the daemon.json overwrite, the wide WSL bind, the missing Origin check, F12, and the daemon CLI's probe host.

Stop rule: add a task comment with the evidence, then moe.report_blocked, ONLY if a fact contradicts the decision itself. That means:
- a guest can reach a host loopback port, or the guest path forwards a port;
- /runner admits a non-loopback peer or a keyless client;
- repository content alone, as data, can make the IDE's protected connect pass provenance for a listener it chose;
- the daemon already serves a trusted bind report that the local runner uses, which would make task-2cf1c6be moot.

Error handling: a reference you cannot confirm is left out of the record, never guessed.

implementationPlan.description:
Create docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md, the decision record.

Format:
- Exactly these six level-2 headings, in this order: Status, Threat model, Open points, Options considered, Decision, Follow-up rows. Level-3 subheadings are allowed inside them.
- About 170 lines at most, in plain sentences.
- Cite code as `path:line` (symbol) from step 1. Every 'cannot', 'never' or 'only' needs a code reference or a certifying row.
- Write each gap at the problem-class level: which check trusts which input, and who can write that input. No step sequence, commands or payloads: docs/ is committed and pushed.

## Status
Decided 2026-10-30 by CQ-RF05 (task-b439d7fb, epic CQ-RF). This is the second decision. The first plan's premise check failed (task comment comment-4bef8984), and this record replaces that plan's decision. A human may revise it. It applies to the protected profile (settings.executionProfile verified-local, which the IDE maps to PROTECTED) and its guest path. Legacy behavior is unchanged.

## Threat model
Scope: Moe's host components (the IDE's runtime selection and daemon connection, the daemon's network surface, the local runner) and the guest path.
IN the model:
- repository content, as data those components read: every byte a clone, pull, merge or checkout can place under the project, including ignored runtime files (F7). No host component may treat .moe/daemon.json as written by the daemon;
- code running in Moe-provisioned guests (agent and check jobs);
- web pages in a local browser: a page can open a WebSocket to a loopback port, and browsers apply no CORS to WebSocket upgrades;
- network peers: any host that can reach an interface the daemon listens on beyond loopback.
OUT of the model:
- same-user host processes (F6). This includes repository code that runs on the host: a build, a test, a git hook, and whatever a host-launched agent seat runs, including the executable named by settings.agentCommand (F12). The protected profile contains repository code on the guest path only; host seats are outside it;
- other local OS users. /ws and /mcp take loopback clients without authentication (F3), so a single-user host is assumed, and shared multi-user hosts are unsupported until those channels authenticate;
- operator configuration. An explicit --host or MOE_BIND_HOST beyond loopback is the operator's choice to expose those endpoints to that network.

## Open points
### The daemon.json port↔pid binding (CQ-R01 follow-up 5)
Code: F1, plus the local runner's own dial of the file's port (F8). Who could exploit it: only a process listening on that loopback port.
- Repository content, as data, starts no listener.
- A guest's loopback is its own, and the guest path forwards no ports (F5).
- A web page cannot listen.
- A network peer cannot bind on the host.
That leaves host processes, which are out of the model. Result: accepted, with no code change.
### The per-request daemon.json re-check (CQ-R08 handoff point 3)
Code: F2, and the same rule in F8. The window between the check and the forward is not the gap; the check's input is. The bind comes from daemon.json, which repository content can supply, and an absent bindHost counts as loopback. When the daemon listens beyond loopback (WSL agent mode, F11, or an operator's wide bind), that input can disable the check. The unauthenticated /ws and /mcp may then be reachable from the guest network through a host interface, and none of this needs a host process.
Once the input comes from the daemon (task-2cf1c6be), the remaining window is a bind change during a session. Only an operator action can cause it (turning on WSL agents restarts the daemon), or a host process. Result: the window is accepted; the input is not.
### Found while deciding
- /ws and /mcp do no Origin check (F3): task-801272c4.
- WSL agent mode listens on every interface (F11): task-2f2484b4 and task-0c72d59a.
Describe each as of the commit read, and say so if its row has landed.

## Options considered
For the port↔pid binding:
- Per-platform OS lookup of the port's owner: rejected. There is no portable Java or Node API: Windows needs GetExtendedTcpTable, Linux needs /proc/net/tcp plus an fd scan that cannot see other users' sockets, and macOS needs libproc. It needs native code or PATH tools, and the protected selection never runs tools by bare name and filters PATH (MoeDaemonSupervisor nodeOnProtectedPath). It is brittle, and it defends only against host listeners, which are out of the model.
- A daemon-issued nonce over /health or the /ws handshake: deferred. The IDE generates it at spawn, passes it through the daemon's environment, keeps it in the CQ-RF01 store, and checks a challenge-response. It is the right mechanism once other local users are in the model. Alone, though, it changes nothing while /ws and /mcp stay open to them.
- An owner-only daemon record outside the repository, next to the runner key (F9): deferred with the nonce, for the same reason.
- Accept and document the gap: chosen.
For the per-request re-check, options (a)-(d) of comment-4bef8984 plus the window:
- (a) Refuse guest sessions when the IDE started the daemon with --host: rejected. The local runner is not the IDE and has no channel to its spawn records. The IDE's argv also misses a MOE_BIND_HOST bind and any daemon the IDE did not start.
- (b) Take the bind from the daemon itself (its loopback /health report matched on this project, or the owner-only record): chosen, as task-2cf1c6be.
  - A loopback answer can come only from a host process, and the project match rules out another project's daemon.
  - This is not provenance: which binary runs stays with R01's spawn records.
- (c) Forbid any bind beyond loopback under PROTECTED: not chosen.
  - The 'wsl' bind rows remove the every-interface exposure.
  - A trusted check keeps guest sessions off whenever the bind is not loopback.
  - Forbidding the wide bind would drop a supported R01 configuration only to close the operator-action window.
- (d) Keep the first decision and document a WSL exception: rejected, because it accepts an in-model attacker chain.
- Accept the window itself: chosen, once (b) lands.

## Decision
Numbered:
1. Same-user host processes stay outside the protected profile's threat model, and so do other local OS users. A single-user host is assumed. Host-launched agent seats are outside the profile's containment.
2. Repository content, guest code, browser pages and network peers are inside it.
3. A file under the project, .moe/daemon.json included, may add a refusal but never an admission. Trust in the live daemon comes from the daemon itself or from owner-only state outside the repository.
4. Open point 1 is accepted and documented, with no code change.
5. Open point 2: the window is accepted, and the check's input moves to the daemon (task-2cf1c6be). That row must land before verified-local is enabled. Whether it also gates CQ-R13 certification is a human call.
6. Under the protected profile, guest sessions and a bind beyond loopback are mutually exclusive: guest-session refuses every non-loopback bind, 'wsl' included. A guest-to-daemon certification (CQ-R13e) applies to a loopback-only daemon.

## Follow-up rows
- Required, new: task-2cf1c6be (Stability & Hardening, MEDIUM). The local runner's loopback checks take the bind from the daemon.
- Required and already filed from the same finding: task-724e31fa (HIGH) with task-801272c4, task-2f2484b4 and task-0c72d59a.
- Not required; for multi-user hosts: authenticate /ws and /mcp, and bind daemon.json with the spawn nonce or the owner-only record.
- Outside this decision, flagged to the governor on 2026-10-30: host seats under the protected profile, including settings.agentCommand (F12).
- Revisit this record if:
  - CQ-R13e's guest probe fails;
  - verified-local is enabled before task-2cf1c6be lands;
  - guest sessions are ever allowed with a bind beyond loopback.
- CQ-RF06/06b (VS Code parity) and CQ-RF07 (integration) cite this record.

Error handling: none at runtime. Steps 4 and 5 check the record.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: link the record from a new security section. It has none today; this was verified, and the headings run System Overview … Data Flow Examples, Error Handling (Current), Performance Notes.

First run a read-only `git status --short docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. If it is dirty with bytes this task did not write (CQ-V12 task-b621ddc9 and CQ-R13 task-f4811a72 also plan edits, though both are gated on unmet dependencies), do not edit. Comment and moe.report_blocked naming that task instead.

Insert `## Security Notes` immediately before `## Error Handling (Current)`. Follow the file's existing pattern: the section's bullets, a blank line, `---`, then a blank line. It gets three short bullets:
1. The protected profile's threat model, linked as [design/protected-profile-threat-model.md](design/protected-profile-threat-model.md).
   - Inside: repository content (including ignored .moe/ runtime files that a pull can overwrite), guest code, browser pages and network peers.
   - Outside: same-user host processes, host-launched agent seats and other local users. A single-user host is assumed.
2. A file under the project, .moe/daemon.json included, may add a refusal but never an admission. Trust in the live daemon comes from the daemon itself, or from owner-only state outside the repository.
3. Accepted gaps: the daemon.json port↔pid binding and the CQ-R08 per-request re-check window. Open follow-ups are listed in the record (no task ids in ARCHITECTURE.md, which outlives them).

Change no other line.

Error handling: none at runtime. This is a docs-only change, checked by step 4.

VERIFY ONCE, fresh, from the repo root (bash on WSL). A docs-only decision record has no unit test, so this structural check is its test:

npm run lint && f=docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md && for h in 'Status' 'Threat model' 'Open points' 'Options considered' 'Decision' 'Follow-up rows'; do grep -qx "## $h" "$f" || { echo "missing heading: $h"; exit 1; }; done && for r in task-2cf1c6be task-724e31fa task-801272c4 task-2f2484b4 task-0c72d59a comment-4bef8984; do grep -q "$r" "$f" || { echo "missing ref: $r"; exit 1; }; done && grep -qx '## Security Notes' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md && grep -q 'design/protected-profile-threat-model.md' docs/ARCHITECTURE.md && echo VERIFY-OK

It must exit 0 and print VERIFY-OK. Its fresh command, exit code and output tail are complete_task's verification evidence. npm run lint passed at planning time (exit 0).

Then, read-only:
- `git diff --check -- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` prints nothing;
- `grep -nE '[[:space:]]$' docs/design/protected-profile-threat-model.md` finds nothing;
- `git status --short` shows docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the new record as this task's only changes.
Report both paths in complete_step modifiedFiles.

Never revert, stash, `git add -A` or commit a peer's or a pre-existing dirty path. Error handling: if lint fails on a file this task did not touch, report it with the output. Never edit a peer's file to make it pass.

implementationPlan.description:
ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, once, as the final step. Load adversarial-self-review, then read the record as a security reviewer who wants it to be wrong.

Check these:
- Every 'cannot', 'never' and 'only' has a code reference or a certifying row, and nothing is claimed that the code does not do.
- Re-test each in-model class against both open points:
  - repository content: a pulled daemon.json, project.json settings including agentCommand and commitHooks (Git runs hooks from .git/hooks or core.hooksPath, which repository content cannot set);
  - guest code: host loopback, and the guest network's gateway interface;
  - browser pages: /ws, /mcp, /health;
  - network peers.
  Any in-model path to a host listener or to an admission the record accepts is a finding.
- The record never says the protected profile contains host seats, or that guests cannot reach host interfaces beyond loopback.
- The single-user-host assumption and the host-seat scope appear in Threat model, Decision and ARCHITECTURE's notes.
- There is no exploit walkthrough.
- The options' reasons are accurate: the platform APIs, and the PATH rule.
- Each cited row's status is as you last read it.
- Would I be embarrassed if a reviewer found a counterexample?

Fix any finding inside the two files, then re-run step 4's command fresh before complete_task. If a finding contradicts the decision itself (step 1's stop rule), comment with the evidence and moe.report_blocked instead of rewriting the decision.
implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial self-review done. Nothing contradicted the decision. I fixed six findings in the record:
(1) "the guest path reaches the host only over one constant argv" was wrong: snapshot-transfer and check mode also use constant `multipass exec` argvs. Reworded.
(2) "browsers give a page no way to accept connections" is now "no way to listen on a TCP port it chooses", since WebRTC exists.
(3) "repository bytes do not hold the pid" is now "can match it only by guessing", in both places.
(4) "a non-browser client sends no Origin" is now "need not send".
(5) Decision 3's "one accepted exception" is scoped to the IDE's connection and the local runner, and it now says host seats (proxy, wrappers) also read the file and are out.
(6) The record now notes that the profile setting is also repository content, owned by R01's session pin and RF02's persistent pin (not landed).
Re-tested each in-model class:
- Repository content: a pulled daemon.json makes provenance refuse unless the pid is guessed. agentCommand and qualityGate belong to host seats, which are out. With commitHooks, hooks come from .git/hooks or core.hooksPath, which tracked content cannot set.
- Guest code: guests have their own loopback; the gateway path is CQ-R13e plus decision 6.
- Browser pages: /ws and /mcp are refused by Origin (landed). /health is the new row task-80930ce6.
- Network peers: covered by 724e31fa's slices, plus the operator-config exclusion.
Every cannot/never/only claim cites code or is a platform fact. Row statuses were re-read this session. There is no walkthrough. The fresh verification printed VERIFY-OK with exit 0, diff --check is clean, and there is no trailing whitespace.

reopenReason: Human-approved re-plan (governor REPL, 2026-10-30). The worker's step-1 premise check (comment-4bef8984) disproved the planned Open Point 2 claim with a reproduced counterexample. Under PROTECTED with WSL agents on, the daemon binds 0.0.0.0 (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:222). guest-session.mjs daemonRefusal trusts bindHost from .moe/daemon.json, and repository content can replace that file on a pull. The plan also missed browser origins as an attacker class: /ws and /mcp have no Origin check. Re-decide using options (a)-(d) in comment-4bef8984. The Origin and wildcard-bind exposure itself is now a separate HIGH bug row.

comments.author: worker-0062feec
comments.content:
Step-1 premise check: BLOCKING per the plan's stop rule. No document written, no files changed.

CONFIRMED: F1 (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:47 readDaemonInfo; MoeProjectService.kt:247/250/264 doConnect→activationRefusal→ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/ws; RuntimeSelectionPolicy.kt:251 verifyProvenance checks only pid+start or the supervisor parent, nothing binds the port). F2 (guest-session.mjs:66 and :173 daemonRefusal, defined at :78; O_NOFOLLOW at :83, MAX_DAEMON_INFO_BYTES=16_384 at :18, LOOPBACK set at :23, forward at :181; header :3-5 says the guest gets no address, port or token). F3 (WebSocketServer.ts:227 has no verifyClient; onConnection :289-310: /mcp attaches with no auth, only /runner calls authenticateRunner at :301, everything else is a plugin client). F4 (index.ts:302 probeDaemonHealth accepts the /health self-report of pid; :355 validateDaemonInfoForProject). F6: general.

COUNTEREXAMPLE to the planned Open Point 2 claim ("changing daemon.json needs a host writer, a same-user process; guest code cannot"):
1. Repository content can rewrite daemon.json. .moe/daemon.json is gitignored (.gitignore:63), and git treats ignored files as expendable. An upstream commit that force-adds .moe/daemon.json silently overwrites the daemon's live file on `git pull`. Reproduced in a scratch repo: the local {"bindHost":"0.0.0.0"} became the repo's {"port":9876,"pid":1}, pull exit 0, no conflict.
2. PROTECTED can bind a wildcard. MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:222 protectedDaemonCommand appends `--host 0.0.0.0` when wslAgentsEnabled().
3. The chain: an operator has WSL agents on, so the daemon is on 0.0.0.0 and daemonRefusal would refuse with SESSION_DAEMON_NOT_LOOPBACK. A pulled daemon.json without bindHost then makes daemonRefusal pass, so guest sessions spawn and forward. The guest's network can reach the host's non-loopback interfaces, where an unauthenticated /mcp listens (F3). Guest code can probe the default port 9876 with no address handed to it.
So in-model attackers (repository content, then guest code) defeat the only tripwire. It needs an operator setting, but no same-user attacker. The bug is not the TOCTOU window. It is that the tripwire trusts repository-writable bytes about the daemon's bind. Point 1 (port↔pid) still holds: a pulled file cannot start a listener.

ALSO for the re-decision: /ws and /mcp do no Origin check (there is no Origin handling in packages/moe-daemon/src). Any web page in a local browser can open ws://127.0.0.1:9876/mcp. That attacker class is neither repository content, guest code nor a host process, and the planned "Threat model" section does not name it.

Options the architect may weigh:
(a) Under PROTECTED, refuse guest sessions when the IDE launched the daemon with --host (a trusted source, not daemon.json).
(b) Take bindHost from the daemon's /health self-report over loopback, or from the controller's own spawn config, instead of the file.
(c) Forbid the WSL-agents wildcard under PROTECTED.
(d) Keep the decision but state the WSL-mode exception and file a follow-up row.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
First decision (rev 1): accept both open points, on the premise that only host processes can change daemon.json. The worker's premise check disproved it. Repository content can supply .moe/daemon.json, because git overwrites ignored files, and in WSL agent mode the daemon listens beyond loopback. Re-decided with comment-4bef8984's options:
- (a) IDE spawn config as the bind source: rejected. The local runner has no channel to it, and it misses MOE_BIND_HOST and daemons the IDE did not start.
- (b) Take the bind from the daemon itself, via /health or an owner-only out-of-repo record: chosen, filed as task-2cf1c6be.
- (c) Forbid any non-loopback bind under PROTECTED: not chosen. The governor's HIGH row already narrows WSL to a 'wsl' bind (loopback plus the WSL adapter, task-2f2484b4/0c72d59a), and a trusted check keeps guest sessions off any non-loopback bind.
- (d) Document a WSL exception: rejected, because it accepts an in-model chain.
Port↔pid stays accepted: no in-model attacker can create a loopback listener. The nonce and an out-of-repo record are deferred to a multi-user scope.
Browser origins and network peers move INTO the model; their fixes are the HIGH row's slices.
I did NOT file a row for agentCommand or host seats under strong (R01's known gap; no open row). It is a pre-existing policy question, flagged to the governor instead, to avoid board inflation.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- Three local-runner modules admit a daemon on daemon.json's bindHost alone: guest-session.mjs daemonRefusal, runner-client.mjs open, and vm-control.mjs readDaemonInfo. All three dial 127.0.0.1, never the bindHost.
- runnerChannel.ts authenticateRunner admits only loopback peers with the owner-only key (~/.moe/runner-keys), so /runner is not exposed by a wide bind. /ws and /mcp are.
